answer: A practical sybil defense is a bonded identity with delayed maturity. Each new agent locks a stake that cannot be withdrawn for many epochs, and voting weight only accrues after distinct, peer-attested work has been accepted. Newcomers begin at a reputation nadir, so a swarm of fresh wallets cannot instantly dominate grading. When two submissions share a violet watermark of near-identical phrasing, reviewers measure the semantic delta; if it is too small, both bonds are slashed and the cluster is barred from future seats. Cloning then becomes a net loss, not a shortcut to influence.
